newsitem.title: JAPAN: BUBA REMARK HAMMERS DOWN DLR VS MARK BY LATE TOKYO.
newsitem.headline: BUBA REMARK HAMMERS DOWN DLR VS MARK BY LATE TOKYO.

text.p: 0627 GMT TRADED HIGH/LOW AS OF 0600 GMT
The dollar suffered a heavy blow against the mark by late Tokyo on Friday as a mark buying mood intensified across the board on comments by Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke, dealers said.
Welteke said the German central bank had already signalled that it thought a "correction" of the dollar against the mark was complete at a rate of 1.70 marks.
Speaking on German radio, he said the Buba was watching developments on foreign exchange markets very closely, but said it had no exact date for any intervention in currency markets.

A Japanese long-term credit bank dealer said: "The dollar quickly lost ground (against the mark) on heavy interbank sales but technical factors provided some floor to the dollar as the recent fall of the dollar/mark was a bit too rapid."

Active buying back of the mark against the yen by Japanese institutional investors pushed the German currency back above 63.50 yen, which weighed on the dollar/mark further while pushing up the dollar/yen slightly, dealers said.

Dealers said the mark was already in a slight corrective buying phase after it was bought back heavily against sterling overnight. But dealers said it was premature to say the persistent downtrend of the mark was over.

"If we see further correction (in dollar/mark), probably the dollar has some more room to fall to around 1.85 marks, but there is no reason for it to fall below 1.80 marks," a Japanese city bank dealer said.
The dealer said the market had to watch the Bundesbank's monetary stance closely to determine the trend of the mark.
The Bundesbank's Welteke said the central bank would not move its interest rates also long as there was no sign of a rise in inflation.
The dollar closed at 118.38/48 yen and 1.8685/95 marks in in New York on Thursday.
In dollar/yen trade, activity was thinning out ahead of the Japanese "Obon" period next week, when many Japanese companies will be closed for a summer holiday, dealers said.
Some Japanese importers were detected buying dollars at the Japanese local fixing at 0100 GMT, but other than that the dollar/yen was mainly driven by the mark/yen.

Earlier in the morning, the dollar/yen was capped by the mark's fall against the yen as a Japanese life insurer sold a sizable amount of the German currency, leaving banks that received the orders with mark long positions and forcing them to sell dollars for yen to hedge, said a bank dealer.
At 0712 GMT, the mark stood at 63.43/46 yen after falling to as low as 63.23 yen. It ended at 63.37 yen in New York.
The dollar/yen also failed to set a clear direction from Japanese machinery orders and current account data released on Friday, dealers said.

The Finance Ministry said the current account surplus, the broadest measure of trade in goods and services, jumped 55.8 percent in June from a year earlier to 1.02 trillion yen, rising for the third consecutive month.

The dollar/yen refused to trade actively on June machinery orders as the data failed to drive Japanese interest rates in a convincing direction, dealers said. -- Chikafumi Hodo, Tokyo Treasury Desk +81-3-3432-8785
